In mathematics, a '''double affine braid group''' is a [[group (mathematics)|group]] containing the [[braid group]] of an [[affine Weyl group]].  Their group rings have quotients  called [[double affine Hecke algebra]]s in the same way that the group rings of [[affine braid group]]s have quotients that are [[affine Hecke algebra]]s.

For affine ''A''<sub>''n''</sub> groups, the double affine braid group is the [[fundamental group]] of the space of ''n'' distinct points on a 2-dimensional torus.
